outroLine: How many did you get? Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: Welcome back, quiz friends! Grab a pen and keep score. Fifty questions, from easy to legend. If you get forty right, your memory is excellent. Let's go! Which animal is the tallest in the world?
lines.a: The giraffe! Its neck alone is about two metres long.

lines.q: Which is the largest mammal on Earth?
lines.a: The blue whale! Bigger than any dinosaur we know of.

lines.q: What is the capital of Egypt?
lines.a: Cairo! It sits right on the river Nile.

lines.q: Which ocean lies between Europe and America?
lines.a: The Atlantic! The second largest ocean on Earth.

lines.q: Who wrote the play Hamlet?
lines.a: William Shakespeare! To be, or not to be.

lines.q: How many colours are in a rainbow?
lines.a: Seven! Red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

lines.q: In which country is the Taj Mahal?
lines.a: India! An emperor built it in memory of his wife.

lines.q: Who was known as the Iron Lady?
lines.a: Margaret Thatcher! A Soviet newspaper gave her that nickname.

lines.q: Which singer recorded the song Jolene?
lines.a: Dolly Parton! She wrote it herself, too.

lines.q: How many legs does an insect have?
lines.a: Six! Spiders have eight, so they're not insects at all.

lines.q: Now it gets a little harder. What is the capital of Portugal?
lines.a: Lisbon! One of the oldest cities in Western Europe.

lines.q: Who painted the famous Water Lilies?
lines.a: Claude Monet! He painted the pond in his own garden at Giverny.

lines.q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
lines.a: Your skin! The liver is the largest one inside you. Sneaky one, I know.

lines.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
lines.a: Mercury! It was once in nearly every thermometer.

lines.q: Who first climbed Mount Everest, together with Tenzing Norgay?
lines.a: Edmund Hillary! In May nineteen fifty-three.

lines.q: Which nineteen thirty-nine film features Rhett Butler?
lines.a: Gone with the Wind! Clark Gable played him.

lines.q: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
lines.a: Six! A bass guitar usually has just four.

lines.q: In which country was paper invented?
lines.a: China! Around two thousand years ago.

lines.q: Who wrote the novel nineteen eighty-four?
lines.a: George Orwell! It gave us the phrase Big Brother.

lines.q: Sunlight helps your body make which vitamin?
lines.a: Vitamin D! Great for strong bones.

lines.q: Welcome to the hard round. Which is the smallest ocean in the world?
lines.a: The Arctic Ocean! Much of it is covered in ice.

lines.q: What is the capital of Morocco?
lines.a: Rabat! Not Casablanca, which is the biggest city. That one catches so many people.

lines.q: Who made the first successful polio vaccine?
lines.a: Jonas Salk! It was declared safe in nineteen fifty-five.

lines.q: In which year did Elizabeth the Second become queen?
lines.a: Nineteen fifty-two! Her coronation came a year later.

lines.q: Which planet has the Great Red Spot?
lines.a: Jupiter! It's a giant storm, wider than Earth. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: Who composed the opera The Magic Flute?
lines.a: Mozart! He wrote it in the last year of his life.

lines.q: Who played Rick in the film Casablanca?
lines.a: Humphrey Bogart! Here's looking at you, kid.

lines.q: What is the chemical symbol for silver?
lines.a: A G! From the Latin word argentum. Gold is A U.

lines.q: Which is the longest river in Europe?
lines.a: The Volga! The Danube is only second.

lines.q: Which country did the band ABBA come from?
lines.a: Sweden! They won Eurovision in nineteen seventy-four with Waterloo.

lines.q: Now it gets very hard. What is the capital of Pakistan?
lines.a: Islamabad! Karachi is much bigger, but it isn't the capital.

lines.q: How many teeth does an adult usually have?
lines.a: Thirty-two! That includes the four wisdom teeth.

lines.q: Who was the first to reach India by sea from Europe, in fourteen ninety-eight?
lines.a: Vasco da Gama! He sailed around the southern tip of Africa.

lines.q: In which year did the Wright brothers make their first flight?
lines.a: Nineteen oh three! The first flight lasted just twelve seconds.

lines.q: Which is the largest island in the world?
lines.a: Greenland! Australia counts as a continent, sorry Australia.

lines.q: Who wrote the novel War and Peace?
lines.a: Leo Tolstoy! More than half a million words long.

lines.q: Which instrument did Louis Armstrong play?
lines.a: The trumpet! His nickname was Satchmo.

lines.q: What is the most common element in the universe?
lines.a: Hydrogen! Stars are mostly made of it.

lines.q: Who played Cleopatra in the nineteen sixty-three film?
lines.a: Elizabeth Taylor! One of the most expensive films ever made.

lines.q: In which year was Magna Carta sealed?
lines.a: Twelve fifteen! King John sealed it at Runnymede.

lines.q: Welcome to the legend round! Which country has three capital cities?
lines.a: South Africa! Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.

lines.q: Who was the first Roman emperor?
lines.a: Augustus! Julius Caesar was never emperor.

lines.q: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
lines.a: The stapes, deep in your ear! Only about three millimetres long.

lines.q: Who discovered the planet Uranus?
lines.a: William Herschel! In seventeen eighty-one, from his garden in Bath.

lines.q: In which year did the Suez Canal open?
lines.a: Eighteen sixty-nine! The Panama Canal followed in nineteen fourteen.

lines.q: Who composed Bolero?
lines.a: Maurice Ravel! Torvill and Dean skated to it in nineteen eighty-four.

lines.q: Which mammal has the longest pregnancy?
lines.a: The African elephant! Almost two years.

lines.q: Three left, stay with me! Who was the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic?
lines.a: Amelia Earhart! In nineteen thirty-two.

lines.q: How many time zones does Russia have?
lines.a: Eleven! From the Baltic Sea to the Pacific.

lines.q: Last one. Which country was the first to let women vote in national elections?
lines.a: New Zealand! In eighteen ninety-three. Finland was first in Europe.
